name: 应敌
prompt: Create a square ink-wash game card artwork for 应敌, a basic unarmed attack in a Chinese cultivation game. The aesthetic is expressive figurative abstraction, dramatic tension and evocative imagery, NOT a detailed character illustration and NOT arbitrary brush marks. One anonymous martial human silhouette lunges diagonally into a decisive punch. Small faceless head bowed, a compact hunched shoulder mass, one unmistakable clenched fist as the main focal shape, long grounded rear leg and bent leading leg forming a taut triangular stance. The figure is built from only 8-12 bold black ink masses and dry-brush strokes, with enough negative-space separations to read arm, fist, torso and legs. Anatomically plausible but intentionally simplified and slightly exaggerated for force. No eyes, face, hair details, garment seams, decorative costume or portrait. Fist and arm are solid legible silhouettes; the trailing lower robe dissolves into textured flying-white dry-brush. Asymmetric dynamic composition, figure fills central 75 percent with breathing room, force driven toward upper right. Restrained pale gray ink wash counterweight behind the figure, a single tiny vermilion brush accent at the striking wrist. Warm off-white rice paper, predominantly monochrome sumi-e, sophisticated raw calligraphic energy, strong white negative space, handmade traditional Chinese martial ink painting. No letters, no seal, no borders, no circular halo, no speed-line comic graphics, no photorealism, no anime face. At small size it should evoke 'a person driving a punch' before any detail is seen. One image only.
